# Gaps between Chapter 5's service contracts and the compiler, found by
# FuzzServiceGenericRequirement: a member-local generic contract whose Effect
# requirement depends on the member's own type parameter through Exclude. tsc
# accepts each cell's twin; the compiler reports EK3101 ("looks up
# Exclude<Req, Request> each time it is called, but ... allows only
# Exclude<Req, Request>"). A key names the rule and the host; under a Layer
# every member form and contract declaration fails alike, and in a const
# annotated Context.Service.Shape<typeof Server> only an explicitly generic
# arrow fails. Contracts written Req or Req | Logger pass everywhere.
# target                       key                              owner     what is missing
FuzzServiceGenericRequirement  exclude/layer-effect  compiler  Chapter 5: tsc accepts serve<Req = never>(handler) returning an Effect that needs Exclude<Req, Request>, implemented by providing Request to the handler, in every member form and contract declaration, under Layer.effect; the compiler reports EK3101 that the member looks up a requirement the contract allows; lane cv-alchemy-returns
FuzzServiceGenericRequirement  exclude/layer-succeed  compiler  Chapter 5: as exclude/layer-effect under Layer.succeed; EK3101; lane cv-alchemy-returns
FuzzServiceGenericRequirement  exclude/annotated/shape  compiler  Chapter 5: as exclude/layer-effect for an explicitly generic arrow <Req>(handler) => ... in a const annotated Context.Service.Shape<typeof Server> (the Shape is the type an implementation has); EK3101, while the contextually typed forms pass; lane cv-alchemy-returns
